newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-Nomura directors arrested over scandal--Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Nomura directors arrested over scandal--Jiji.

text.p: Prosecutors have arrested former executives of scandal-hit Nomura Securities Co Ltd over suspected violations of the nation's commercial code, Jiji news agency reported on Wednesday.

On Tuesday, Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), filed a criminal complaint with prosecutors alleging that Nomura, two former executives and a former general manager compensated a client for investment losses.

In late March, prosecutors said that the client was linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer. Sokaiya extort money from a company by threatening to disturb shareholders' meetings, and Japan's commercial law has prohibited payoffs to racketeers since 1982.
The Tokyo Prosecutors Office was not available to comment on the Jiji report, but is due to hold a news conference at 4.00 p.m. (0700 GMT).
